content:
The hyperbola trips students who just learned the ellipse. One sign flips, and c² = a² + b² instead of minus. Get that reflex right and the marks follow. Take the free JEE Hyperbola online test below. It has 15 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Aim for 12 out of 15.

What JEE asks from the hyperbola

  • Transverse and conjugate axes from the standard form.
  • Foci and eccentricity using c² = a² + b².
  • Asymptotes and the angle between them.
  • Directrices, latus rectum and focal chords.
  • Position of a point relative to the branches.

Formulas to revise first

  • For x²/a²−y²/b²=1, the foci sit at x = ± c.
  • Here c² = a² + b², so eccentricity e stays above 1.
  • Asymptotes run as y = ± (b/a)x through the centre.
  • The latus rectum length equals 2b²/a, as with the ellipse.
  • The director circle is x² + y² = a² − b², when a exceeds b.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Using minus for c², which belongs to the ellipse.
  • Swapping a and b when the transverse axis turns vertical.
  • Reading the asymptote slope as a/b instead of b/a.

Free JEE Hyperbola online test

The 15-question quiz below comes from our verified DPP question bank. It mirrors the paid e-book exactly. Answer all 15, then press Check my score. Fix the sign slips first, because they cost the most.

How to use this test

Give yourself about 30 minutes. Do the axes and foci first. Those come fast. Then face the asymptote and directrix ones. Write each line by hand. Do not rush the sign. Recall that c uses a plus here. Check that one point before you move on. If a value looks wrong, redo it once. Note every slip you make. Try the set again in two days. Your speed will grow, and your slips will fall.

Practise the whole chapter

Want the full chapter? The JEE Maths DPP Hyperbola e-book holds every worksheet for Rs 49. Each question carries a step-by-step solution, so the method sticks. You can also open the whole JEE Maths DPP e-book shelf, and the practice papers cost Rs 79. Building the full syllabus? The free JEE Maths course at vidaara.org covers the hyperbola end to end. Then this JEE Hyperbola online test shows what stuck.

quiz.title: JEE Hyperbola Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen exam-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: For the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1, the transverse and conjugate axes are:
questions.explanation: The transverse axis is 2a = 8 (along the positive term) and the conjugate axis is 2b = 6.

questions.q: The foci of x²/225 − y²/64 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: For a hyperbola c = √(a² + b²) = √(225 + 64) = 17. So the foci are (± 17, 0).

questions.q: The asymptotes of x²/256 − y²/900 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: The asymptotes satisfy x²/a² − y²/b² = 0, giving y = ± (b/a)x = ± (15/8)x.

questions.q: The distance between the directrices of x²/400 − y²/441 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: The directrices are x = ± a²/c, so the distance is 2a²/c. With a² = 400 and c = 29, that gives 800/29.

questions.q: The director circle of x²/1296 − y²/225 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: The director circle is x² + y² = a² − b² = 1296 − 225 = 1071, valid because a² exceeds b².

questions.q: The endpoints of the latus rectum through the focus (26, 0) of x²/100 − y²/576 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: At x = c = 26 the equation gives y = ± b²/a = ± 576/10 = ± 288/5. So the endpoints are (26, ± 288/5).

questions.q: The foci of x²/36 − y²/64 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: For a hyperbola c = √(a² + b²) = √(36 + 64) = 10. So the foci are (± 10, 0).

questions.q: For the hyperbola x²/441 − y²/400 = 1, the transverse and conjugate axes are:
questions.explanation: The transverse axis is 2a = 42 (along the positive term) and the conjugate axis is 2b = 40.

questions.q: The asymptotes of x²/576 − y²/49 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: The asymptotes satisfy x²/a² − y²/b² = 0, giving y = ± (b/a)x = ± (7/24)x.

questions.q: The foci of x²/81 − y²/1600 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: For a hyperbola c = √(a² + b²) = √(81 + 1600) = 41. So the foci are (± 41, 0).

questions.q: The director circle of x²/900 − y²/256 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: The director circle is x² + y² = a² − b² = 900 − 256 = 644, valid because a² exceeds b².

questions.q: The distance between the directrices of x²/64 − y²/225 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: Distance = 2a²/c with a² = 64 and c = 17. So it equals 128/17.

questions.q: For the hyperbola x²/64 − y²/36 = 1, the point (5, 3) lies:
questions.explanation: Compute 25/64 − 9/36 − 1, which is negative. A negative value places the point in the region between the branches, so outside.

questions.q: For the hyperbola x²/576 − y²/100 = 1, the transverse and conjugate axes are:
questions.explanation: The transverse axis is 2a = 48 (along the positive term) and the conjugate axis is 2b = 20.

questions.q: The product of the perpendicular distances from any point of x²/2304 − y²/196 = 1 to its asymptotes is:
questions.explanation: This product equals a²b²/(a² + b²) = (2304)(196)/2500 = 112896/625, constant for every point on the curve.
